Iowa law sets out when a person occupying land can claim title by adverse possession, and how an owner can remove someone who has no right to be there.

What the official sources say

  • Actions brought for the recovery of real property must be commenced within ten years (the limitation underlying Iowa adverse possession). (Iowa Code 614.1 (recovery of real property, 10 years); source)
  • Trespass includes entering or remaining on property without justification after being notified orally or in writing, or by conspicuously posted notice, to abstain or vacate by the owner or person in lawful possession. (Iowa Code 716.7(2)(a)(2); source)
  • Summary forcible entry and detainer remedy is available where a defendant entered by force, intimidation, fraud or stealth upon another's prior actual possession and detains it; also for holdover, lease breach, nonpayment of rent, and possession after a valid tax deed. (Iowa Code 648.1; source)
  • Thirty days' peaceable possession with the plaintiff's knowledge after the cause of action accrues bars the forcible entry and detainer proceeding. (Iowa Code 648.18; source)

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Iowa statutes set the basic rules between landlords and tenants, including deposits, notices and what happens when a rental is sold.

What the official sources say

  • A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit in excess of two months' rent. (Iowa Code 562A.12; source)
  • Landlord must return the deposit or give a written statement of reasons for withholding within thirty days from termination of the tenancy and receipt of the tenant's mailing address or delivery instructions. (Iowa Code 562A.12; source)
  • Month-to-month tenancy may be terminated by either party by written notice at least thirty days before the periodic rental date specified in the notice (week-to-week: ten days). (Iowa Code 562A.34(1)-(2); source)
  • Landlord must give at least 24 hours' notice of intent to enter and enter at reasonable times, except in emergency or if impracticable; tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent for inspection, repairs, or showings to purchasers. (Iowa Code 562A.19; source)
  • Landlord must comply with housing codes affecting health and safety, make repairs to keep the premises fit and habitable, and maintain electrical, plumbing, heating and other supplied facilities. (Iowa Code 562A.15(1); source)
  • Retaliation by raising rent, cutting services, or threatening an action for possession after a tenant's code complaint, complaint under 562A.15, or tenant union activity is prohibited; a good-faith complaint within one year creates a presumption of retaliation; tenant may recover damages and attorney fees. (Iowa Code 562A.36; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Iowa law requires a landlord to give a specific written notice before filing an eviction, and the number of days depends on the reason.

What the official sources say

  • Nonpayment: if rent is unpaid when due and the tenant fails to pay within three days after written notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate, the landlord may terminate. (Iowa Code 562A.27(2); source)
  • Material noncompliance with the lease: written notice that the rental agreement will terminate not less than seven days after receipt if the breach is not remedied in seven days. (Iowa Code 562A.27(1); source)
  • No-cause end of month-to-month tenancy: 30 days' written notice; holdover tenants may be sued for possession and, if willful and not in good faith, for actual damages and attorney fees. (Iowa Code 562A.34(2), (4); source)
  • The summary court remedy for eviction is forcible entry and detainer (chapter 648). (Iowa Code 648.1; source)

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

When property tax goes unpaid in Iowa, the statutes allow the taxing authority to sell a lien or the property itself, and they give the owner a set time to redeem.

What the official sources say

  • Iowa sells tax sale certificates (liens) of purchase, with a deed available only after the redemption period; if no bid is received or the bid is below the amount due, the county treasurer bids the total amount due for the county. (Iowa Code 446.19(1); source)
  • A parcel sold at tax sale may be redeemed by paying the county treasurer the sale amount plus certificate fee and interest of two percent per month (each fraction of a month counted as a full month), plus later-year payments with interest. (Iowa Code 447.1(1); source)
  • After one year and nine months from sale (nine months for sales under 446.18; three months for 446.19A/446.19B), the certificate holder may serve notice that the right of redemption expires and a deed will issue unless redeemed within ninety days of completed service. (Iowa Code 447.9(1); source)
  • The county may redeem owner-occupied residential parcels for owners unable to contribute to public revenue, on petition to the board of supervisors. (Iowa Code 447.9(3); source)
  • A summary forcible entry and detainer remedy is available against defendants who remain in possession after issuance of a valid tax deed. (Iowa Code 648.1(6); source)
